source: The rules docs/overrides.md marks settled (build step 3, item 3.1a). The open rules (3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, and the open parts of 6 and 10) have no row: the spec package will carry them, read out of the Windows and Linux executables.

rules.title: A mod's file replaces, whole, the base game's file at the same relative path

evidence.says: The field exists so that a mod can override one event of the unmodded game from a file with another name, and so not override the entire file: a mod file named as the game's file overrides all of it.

rules.note: Holds for paths written exactly alike. Paths that differ only in letter case are rule 9, open. The rule's evidence is about the game/ folder; a mod file at the path of a jomini/, clausewitz/ or DLC file is open (rules 3 and 10).

rules.title: A file is identified by its whole relative path, not by its file name

evidence.source: The base game's files, measured on 1.21.0.3
evidence.where: events/situation_events/debug.txt and events/test_events/debug.txt; music/in_game/music.txt and music/main_themes/music.txt; the two 00_temple_district_buildings.txt under common/buildings
evidence.says: Each pair holds different definitions; if a file name alone identified a file, one of each pair would never be read and the base game would lose, for example, its main-menu themes.

rules.title: A DLC is a folder of game/dlc/ with a descriptor whose path names it; its files sit at their path inside the pack

evidence.source: The Linux executable, its message texts
evidence.where: CDLCManager::InitializeMods(), Folder not found for DLC/Mod %s:, beside clausewitzlib/dlc.cpp
evidence.says: DLCs and mods are handled by one manager with one descriptor reader.

evidence.where: the path key of each descriptor
evidence.says: Each pack's descriptor names its own folder (path = "dlc/dlc003_fp1"), and its files repeat the game's layout inside it.

rules.note: On 1.21.0.3 no DLC file has the relative path of a base-game file or of another pack's, so the order of DLC against the base game decides nothing there. Whether a mod's file at a DLC file's path replaces it is open.

rules.title: An event defined more than once: the largest id_override_priority wins, whole; equal largest values are an error

evidence.says: An event id defined more than once is resolved by id_override_priority, an integer that is 0 by default; the definition with the largest value overrides all the others; two with the same value are an error.
The game reports a duplicated event id with the same override priority.

rules.note: Within one file as across files (rule 11). Which of two equal-priority definitions the game then uses is not stated, so none is named: the index reports a clash.

rules.title: A history character defined more than once: the largest history_override_priority sets the base attributes and birth date; the rest adds up; equal largest values are an error

evidence.says: The same rule with history_override_priority, except that only the character's base attributes (the fields listed above line 25) and the date of birth are overridden; everything else from the definitions adds up.
The game reports a duplicate character id in history.

rules.note: Within one file as across files (rule 11).

rules.title: Every declaration of an on-action, in any file, adds to it

evidence.says: An on-action's data may be declared in several files, and a mod adds effects to a base on-action this way without replacing its file; one on-action may not have more than one trigger or more than one effect block.

rules.note: What happens to an on-action's single values (fallback, fallback_event, weight_multiplier) when two declarations set them is open (experiment 4).

rules.title: Province terrain is not a keyed database: every file is read, each a mix of statements

evidence.says: The folder is not a regular keyed database; every .txt file of it is read in order, by convention the 00_ file holding the terrain and the 01_ file the winter properties.

rules.note: Which of two statements setting the same property is in force depends on the order files are read in (rule 4), which is open.

rules.title: Defines are set field by field: every top-level key is a group, the defines inside it are the definitions, and a group written again sets only the defines it names

evidence.source: The base game's files, measured on 1.21.0.3
evidence.where: 19 groups written in two files each with no define in both, for example NRite in common/defines/00_defines.txt and common/defines/graphic/00_graphics.txt
evidence.says: If a later group replaced the earlier one whole, the base game would lose one half of each.

evidence.source: The Linux executable, its message texts
evidence.where: Looking for a single value %s in %s, but scripted as an array, won't assign until changed, beside clausewitzlib/definesreader.cpp
evidence.says: The defines reader assigns single values.

rules.note: Which value wins when two files set the same define is the order files are read in (rule 4), which is open.

rules.title: Container keys written in several files add up; the definitions are the entries inside them

evidence.source: The base game's files, measured on 1.21.0.3
evidence.says: Each file holds different entries, and dropping all but one file's would leave the base game without most of them.
